content.text: No non-compete covenant exists anywhere in the agreement — I verified the covenants article, licence grants, and the competing-product mechanics.

input.quote: (d) Termination for Competing Product of Sanofi. If after [***]: (i) Sanofi or its Affiliates, alone or with or through a Third Party, develop, manufacture or commercialize a Competing Product and (ii) Sanofi or its Affiliates have not commenced a Registrational Clinical Trial for a Product prior to commencing the activities in Section 12.2(d)(i), RevMed may terminate this Agreement effective [***] after it delivers written notice to Sanofi that it is exercising its rights under this Section 12.2(d)
input.rationale: The agreement contains no covenant restricting Sanofi's business: Article XIII's covenants (13.3 RevMed-only; 13.4 mutual debarment/compliance/pharmacovigilance) impose no competing-activity restriction, and the licence is granted in the "Field", defined as "any and all uses", so there is no field-of-use limit either. The only competing-product mechanic is Section 12.2(d), which is a RevMed termination right (with a cure/election alternative and a carve-out where Sanofi has already commenced a Registrational Clinical Trial for a Product); it does not prohibit Sanofi or its Affiliates from developing, manufacturing or commercialising a Competing Product, and its consequences (Section 12.3(c), p0500 et seq.) are the ordinary reversion package. That trigger belongs to the termination checklist, not NONCOMPETE, and we do not flag the same term twice. The Section 15.2 separation duties at p0614 attach to the acquired party's family only as a condition to excluding acquiror IP "In the case of RevMed" (Sanofi's counterpart at p0612 carries no such conditions), so they are not a restriction on us. This sits at the preferred position; no redline.

mappings.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
